title: What teaching staff and learning outcome requirements must a study program meet for A3ES accreditation in Portugal?
description: A3ES accreditation rules for Portuguese study programs: minimum PhD and specialist staff ratios by cycle, coordinator rules, and required competences.
shortAnswer: In Portugal, every degree-awarding study program must be accredited by the Agência de Avaliação e Acreditação do Ensino Superior (A3ES). Under article 57 of Decree-Law 74/2006, as republished by Decree-Law 65/2018, a program needs its own academically qualified and specialized teaching staff in adequate numbers. For a university bachelor's (licenciatura), at least 60 percent of staff must be career staff, 50 percent must hold a PhD, and 50 percent must be specialized in the program's core areas.
keyTakeaways: Article 57(1) of Decree-Law 74/2006 sets four general requirements: an educational and scientific project, a qualified and specialized teaching staff of adequate size, adequate human and material resources, and compliance with teaching career statutes.

Minimum staff ratios rise by cycle: university licenciatura 60/50/50 percent (career staff, PhDs, specialists), master's 75/60/50 percent, and doctorate 75 percent career staff with all teachers holding a PhD.
Program coordinators must hold a PhD in the core training area (or, in polytechnics, the specialist title) and be career staff of the institution.
The tighter staffing rules from Decree-Law 65/2018 apply to new program requests made after October 15, 2020 and to programs in operation after December 31, 2022.
Learning outcomes are anchored in the legal competences for each degree, such as article 5 for the licenciatura, and A3ES assesses whether teaching delivers them.
regulator: Agência de Avaliação e Acreditação do Ensino Superior (A3ES), the Agency for Assessment and Accreditation of Higher Education
appliesTo: Public and private universities and polytechnic institutions in Portugal
Every study program leading to a licenciatura, mestrado (including integrated master's) or doutoramento
Program coordinators and the technical and scientific bodies that approve teaching staff
Institutions proposing new programs (NCE) and those renewing accreditation of programs in operation (ACEF)

sections.heading: Which laws govern A3ES program accreditation?

blocks.text: Program accreditation rests on four instruments listed on A3ES's [normative framework page](https://a3es.pt/pt/a3es/quadro-normativo/): Decree-Law 369/2007, which created A3ES; Law 38/2007, the legal regime for quality assessment of higher education, amended by Law 94/2019; Law 62/2007, the legal regime of higher education institutions (RJIES); and Decree-Law 74/2006 on degrees and diplomas, amended and republished by Decree-Law 65/2018 and further amended by Decree-Law 27/2021.

A3ES states that it is the body responsible for accrediting the [study programs](https://a3es.pt/en/assessment-and-accreditation/study-programmes/) of Portuguese higher education institutions, and that accreditation covers all institutions and all programs. Its main procedures are assessment of programs in operation (ACEF), prior accreditation of new programs (NCE) and a special renewal procedure for non-aligned programs (PERA).

A3ES consolidates the staffing rules in its guidance [Criteria for the Accreditation of Study Programmes: Qualification of Teaching Staff](https://a3es.pt/wp-content/uploads/Microsoft-Word-Qualification-Criteria-for-Teaching-Staff-2.1-002-Qualification-Criteria-for-Teaching-Staff-2.1.pdf), version 2.1 of June 2021.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the instruments listed by A3ES as at November 2026. The A3ES staffing criteria were last updated in June 2021. Confirm the consolidated text of Decree-Law 74/2006 on Diário da República before relying on a specific article.

sections.heading: What are the general requirements for accrediting a program?

blocks.text: Article 57(1) of [Decree-Law 74/2006 as republished by Decree-Law 65/2018](https://data.dre.pt/eli/dec-lei/65/2018/08/16/p/dre/pt/html) lists four general requirements for accrediting any study program:

items: Its own educational, scientific and cultural project, suited to the program's objectives.
A total teaching staff of its own ("corpo docente total próprio") that is academically qualified, specialized and adequate in number.
The human and material resources needed for the level and quality of training, including teaching spaces, equipment, libraries and laboratories.
Compliance with the teaching career statutes on the percentages of career and invited teachers and the distribution of career staff by category.

blocks.text: Articles 6, 16 and 29 set the special requirements for the licenciatura, master's and doctorate respectively. Article 60 provides that failure to meet the legal requirements or the scientific and pedagogical criteria that justified accreditation leads to its revocation, after the institution is heard, with A3ES setting closure deadlines and safeguards for enrolled students.

sections.heading: What teaching staff ratios does each cycle require?

blocks.text: Each cycle has three minimum percentages, measured in full-time equivalents (FTE): career staff, PhD holders and staff specialized in the program's fundamental training areas. A3ES's criteria summarize them for university education as follows.

blocks.text: Polytechnic programs use the same 60/50/50 percent (licenciatura) and 75/60/50 percent (master's) figures, but the specialist requirement can be met by holders of the specialist title of recognized experience and professional competence as well as by specialized PhDs. Where a program has several fundamental areas, article 6(7) requires specialized staff to be distributed in proportion to the weight of each area.

Two institution-level rules in RJIES sit above the program ratios. Article 47 requires universities to have at least one PhD holder for every 30 students and at least half of those staff full-time. Article 49 requires polytechnics to have at least one specialist or PhD for every 30 students, with at least 15 percent full-time PhD holders and at least 35 percent holding the specialist title.

sections.heading: What rules apply to coordinators and exceptional cases?

blocks.text: Coordinators of university programs at all three cycles must hold a PhD in the program's fundamental training area and be career teaching or research staff of the institution. In polytechnics, the coordinator may instead be a specialist of recognized experience and professional competence, but must still be career staff.

Article 57(5) gives A3ES a narrow discretion for arts programs, fields where qualified academic staff demonstrably do not exist, and multidisciplinary master's and doctoral programs. In those cases A3ES may exceptionally accept lower ratios, allow compliance to be reached progressively in the first years, and, for polytechnic programs, treat as a specialist a degree holder with at least 10 years of professional experience in the area, including at least five effective years in the last 10, and a professional curriculum confirmed by the institution's technical and scientific body.

Transitional rules matter for planning. Under article 4 of Decree-Law 65/2018, as A3ES explains, the revised staffing criteria apply to prior accreditation requests for new programs made after October 15, 2020, and to programs in operation after December 31, 2022, in the third cycle of assessment.

sections.heading: How does A3ES accreditation deal with learning outcomes?

blocks.text: Learning outcomes are set in law as the competences a graduate must demonstrate, and accreditation tests whether the program delivers them. Article 5 of Decree-Law 74/2006 states that the licenciatura is awarded to those who demonstrate:

items: Knowledge and understanding in a field that builds on secondary education and, in some domains, reaches the forefront of the field.
The ability to apply that knowledge with a professional approach.
Problem solving and the ability to construct and support their own arguments.
The ability to gather and interpret relevant information, including social, scientific and ethical aspects.
Communication of information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Learning skills for lifelong learning with a high degree of autonomy.

blocks.text: [Law 38/2007](https://data.dre.pt/eli/lei/38/2007/08/16/p/dre/pt/html), as enacted, lists among its quality assessment parameters the qualification of the teaching staff and its fit with the institution's mission (article 4(1)(b)) and the adequacy of the teaching in each cycle to the competences it must ensure (article 4(2)(a)). In practice, a program needs a traceable line from these legal competences to [measurable learning outcomes](/guides/how-to-write-measurable-learning-outcomes), course units and assessment, of the kind a [curriculum map](/glossary/curriculum-mapping) records.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry starts from the legal competences for each cycle and maps them to program outcomes, course units and assessment points before content is written. Because each unit is tied to a fundamental training area, the same structure shows whether the specialized staff are distributed in proportion to the curriculum.

faqs.q: How long does A3ES accreditation last?
faqs.a: Article 59 of Decree-Law 74/2006, as republished, provides that accreditation is granted for the period set in the accreditation decision under an A3ES regulation, or for one year where accreditation results from tacit approval. The program is reassessed before the period ends, and if no decision has been issued in time, accreditation is extended in successive one year periods.

faqs.q: Can invited or part-time teachers count toward the ratios?
faqs.a: Yes, in proportion to their contract. A3ES counts the total teaching staff in full-time equivalents, with part-time teachers weighted by the percentage of their contract. A3ES also treats a teacher as full-time in an institution only if their main or exclusive teaching activity is there, and a teacher cannot be full-time at more than one institution.

faqs.q: May an institution advertise a program before A3ES accredits it?
faqs.a: No. Article 59-A of Decree-Law 74/2006 prohibits institutions from advertising degree-awarding programs that have not yet been accredited and registered, or whose accreditation has been revoked. Institutions must also list accredited programs on their website with the accreditation date, its period, and the registration number and date.

faqs.q: Do these rules apply to private institutions?
faqs.a: Yes. A3ES accredits programs at all Portuguese higher education establishments, public and private. Some career statute percentages referred to in article 57(1)(d) are framed around the public teaching career statutes, and A3ES says compliance with institution-level percentages is monitored periodically rather than in each program assessment.
